evals.prompt: Analyze interaction data from our platform showing that Student A spends 3x longer on video content than text, completes visual exercises faster, but struggles with purely auditory instructions. What learning profile can we build?
evals.expected_output: A nuanced learning profile analysis that avoids rigid style categorization while identifying actionable content delivery preferences.
assertions: Response identifies visual/multimedia preference patterns without rigidly categorizing the student into a single learning style
Response acknowledges the limitations and debates around learning style theories
Response provides actionable multimodal content delivery recommendations

evals.prompt: A teacher wants to classify all 25 students as either 'visual,' 'auditory,' or 'kinesthetic' learners and create separate content tracks for each group. Evaluate this approach.
evals.expected_output: A critical evaluation explaining why rigid VAK categorization is problematic, with an alternative evidence-based approach.
assertions: Response critically evaluates the VAK model citing current research evidence against rigid categorization
Response explains why separate content tracks based on styles can be counterproductive
Response proposes an alternative approach based on multimodal delivery for all students

evals.prompt: Design a learner preference detection assessment for our educational platform that can adapt content delivery without over-classifying students.
evals.expected_output: An assessment instrument that captures learner preferences across multiple dimensions while avoiding simplistic categorization.
assertions: Assessment captures preferences across multiple dimensions (not just visual/auditory/kinesthetic)
Design avoids binary or rigid style assignments in favor of preference profiles or spectrums
Response includes guidance on how the platform should use results for adaptive content delivery

evals.prompt: Our platform data shows that 40% of 1st ESO students consistently take 2x the expected time to complete modules. Some rush through, others take much longer. How should we analyze and respond to these pacing differences?
evals.expected_output: A pacing analysis framework that identifies different pacing patterns and proposes adaptive responses for each pattern type.
assertions: Response distinguishes between different causes of pacing variation (difficulty, engagement, distraction, mastery level)
Response proposes data analysis methods to identify the root cause of each student's pacing pattern
Response recommends adaptive pacing strategies rather than one-size-fits-all time adjustments

evals.prompt: Apply Gardner's multiple intelligences framework to recommend content adaptations for a 4th Primaria unit on the water cycle. How can the same content engage different intelligence profiles?
evals.expected_output: Content adaptation recommendations across multiple intelligence dimensions with critical awareness of the framework's limitations.
assertions: Response provides specific content variations for at least 4 different intelligence dimensions (linguistic, spatial, kinesthetic, naturalist, etc.)
Response acknowledges the scientific debate around Gardner's theory while still offering practical applications
All content variations maintain the same core learning objectives about the water cycle
